description: Conjecture-driven Hamiltonian campaign. Jx and Jy are the unscaled collective couplings; the Hamiltonian uses Jx/sqrt(N_pixel) and Jy/sqrt(N_pixel).

cases.conditions: B1 exact matching; B2 independent central X/Y channels; test B3 reciprocity.
cases.hypothesis: Exact hz0=hz matching supplies extensive flip resonances, while X and Y coupling removes meridional locking; this is the cleanest new Born candidate.

cases.conditions: B1 exact matching; B2 detector XX/YY anisotropy plus central X/Y mixing; test B3.
cases.hypothesis: Weak noncommuting detector exchange broadens the resonant graph without overwhelming the matched Ising energy structure.

cases.conditions: B1 broadened matching; B2 disorder smooths coherent atoms while X/Y mixes; test B3.
cases.hypothesis: Weak field disorder should smooth finite-size spectral atoms while leaving the matched resonant window intact; excessive disorder would destroy B1.

cases.conditions: B1 retained but HT3/B2 intentionally weakened by sparse end coupling.
cases.hypothesis: Restricting the central qubit to chain ends should reduce resonant-graph extension and azimuthal mixing, separating energy matching from collective mixing.

cases.conditions: HT1 small denominators at the Jpm band edge; HT2-HT3 exchange graph; disorder probes HT5 smoothing.
cases.hypothesis: At hz=Jpm the exchange band edge supplies many small detunings; weak field disorder should fill phase gaps and reduce coherent atoms without erasing the tail.

cases.conditions: HT1-HT3 exchange-band resonance at hz=0; weak bond disorder tests coherent-block versus stable-law behavior.
cases.hypothesis: The band center maximizes accessible exchange transitions; weak Jpm disorder should suppress repeated eigenvalues and reveal whether the inverse-square tail survives incoherent mixing.

cases.conditions: B1-B2 matching and X/Y mixing plus HT1-HT4 exchange-induced small denominators.
cases.hypothesis: Jpm=J combines the strongest heavy-tail family with exact central matching; it should expose a finite-range r^-2 shoulder followed by any Born r^-4 crossover.

cases.conditions: Tests why exact degeneracy without HT2-HT3 extension is insufficient.
cases.hypothesis: Repeated isolated dimers create exact or near degeneracies but fragmented projected blocks; the output should remain atomic or nonuniversal despite a large raw degeneracy count.

cases.conditions: B1 approximate matching with explicit detector noncommutation; B2 enhanced mixing.
cases.hypothesis: A weak detector transverse field should break the meridional symmetry while perturbing, rather than destroying, the matched transition manifold.

cases.conditions: Maximizes HT3 connectivity and B2 mixing while changing energy extensivity.
cases.hypothesis: All-to-all geometry tests whether connectivity alone improves Born reciprocity or instead produces coherent collective modes and spectral atoms.

cases.conditions: Conserves total Sz and tests whether sector-resolved HT conditions survive a different central coupling.
cases.hypothesis: Central flip-flop exchange can create exact energy exchange but may remain symmetry-sector locked; it distinguishes resonance from full qubit-state mixing.

cases.conditions: Directly probes HT1 finite-time window and HT4 pole reach on both sides of a resonance.
cases.hypothesis: Fine detuning around the exchange band edge should reveal a width set by max(1/t,g||V||res), not a singular effect at one exact hz value.
